page: Amazon Web Services c5.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8275CL processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, provisioned with 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated virtual execution threads. Its cache hierarchy consists of 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX and AVX-512F for vector processing, alongside cryptographic AES acceleration.

The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per thread. Networking is provisioned at a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external networked block storage for persistent data, and features no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark testing places the instance predominantly in the mid-range relative to comparable hardware. It scores 1,190 in Geekbench single-core and 7,460 in multi-core metrics, with code compilation reaching 13,903. PassMark evaluation yields a CPU mark of 16,486.15 and a memory rating of 2,542.7. Uncached sequential memory throughput registers at 79.46 GB/sec for reads and 47.95 GB/sec for writes. In application-level benchmarks, the instance sustains 15.23 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.86 GB/sec in static web serving. Processing smaller language models yields 763.39 prompt tokens per second, but medium 7B models show weaker prompt evaluation throughput at 22.69 tokens per second.

Because memory is constrained to 2.0 GB per vCPU and local storage is absent, the instance is structurally aligned with compute-heavy, memory-light tasks rather than data caching or large in-memory footprints. Optimal workloads include distributed batch computing, software compilation pipelines, media encoding, static web delivery, and backend processing queues where high instruction throughput is prioritized over resource density.
